lore: Built in a cave in Afghanistan from salvaged Stark Industries weapons, the Mark I was Tony's desperate bid for survival. Crude and heavy — it was the seed of everything that followed.
The first full-flight suit, built in Tony's Malibu workshop. It proved the concept of repulsor-driven flight but iced up at altitude — a flaw that drove every suit that followed.
The first fully combat-ready suit and the template for all that followed. Its iconic red and gold palette became synonymous with Iron Man.
An iterative refinement of the Mark III, worn while Tony was being slowly poisoned by his own arc reactor. It served as his primary suit during the Hammer Expo attack.
Designed for portability, the Mark V folds into a briefcase and deploys in seconds. A sacrifice in durability for unmatched accessibility.
Powered by a new triangular arc reactor using Tony's self-synthesised element, the Mark VI solved the palladium poisoning crisis and debuted at the Stark Expo battle.
Designed with wristband-actuated auto-deploy, the Mark VII allowed Tony to suit up in freefall. It survived the Chitauri invasion and a nuclear missile ride through the wormhole.
The first suit of Tony's obsessive post-Avengers build phase. Part of the Iron Legion deployed against Aldrich Killian's Extremis soldiers.
Deployed remotely during the Iron Legion activation sequence. Destroyed during the Malibu mansion assault or the Killian confrontation.
A darker variant built with low-observable materials as Tony explored stealth configurations within the Legion series.
An extended-range weapons configuration, Longbow was built to engage threats from a distance before they reached Tony's position.
A heavier-plated variant trading agility for resilience, designed to sustain punishment in sustained firefights.
A load-bearing variant built with reinforced framing to handle extreme structural stress — part rescue suit, part battering ram.
Built around an overclocked arc reactor configuration, the Mark XIV channels higher energy output at the cost of thermal stability.
Tony's first dedicated stealth suit, built with radar-absorbent plating and a suppressed arc reactor signature. What it lacks in firepower it makes up for in invisibility.
A sleek black-and-crimson variant optimised for night operations, with enhanced low-light sensor arrays and minimal light emission.

power_source: Arc Reactor Mark II (High-Output Chest Configuration)
lore: Built around a massively oversized chest arc reactor for maximum energy-beam output. The heaviest pre-Igor suit, designed to punch through reinforced structures.
A well-rounded suit with a polished silver trim — no extreme specialisation, just refinement. Tony's most balanced Legion-era build.
An agility-focused suit with striking orange-and-black colouring and a pursuit-optimised aerodynamic profile. Built to run down fast-moving targets.
The Python's dark green finish and flexible joint design allowed it to navigate confined spaces and execute extreme manoeuvres other suits couldn't manage.
All gold. Tony built the Midas as a fully gold-titanium variant — partly an aesthetic experiment, partly to test different alloy ratios. Everything Stark touches turns to gold.
One of the fastest suits in the Legion series, Hot Rod's deep crimson and chrome livery screamed speed before it even moved. Built for high-speed intercept missions.
The Shades featured tinted sensor arrays and a deep maroon-grey finish that made it difficult to track visually. A balance of stealth and combat capability.
The Tank earned its name. Clad in the heaviest armour plating of the Legion series, it could absorb direct missile hits and keep operating. Slow, but nearly indestructible.
The Thumper's heavily reinforced gauntlets deliver seismic impact strikes, built for opponents requiring raw kinetic force rather than energy weapons.
Purpose-built with radiation hardening and hazmat containment capabilities. The Gamma could operate safely in nuclear or radiological environments.
The mirror-chrome Disco is exactly what it sounds like — a fully polished suit that reflects light in all directions. Tony clearly had a sense of humour when naming this one.
An all-rounder with a distinctive burnt-orange and black finish. Jack was Tony's compact combat variant — no extreme specialisations, just excellent fundamentals.
The Fiddler was built with acoustic dampening systems to minimise sound signature — a suit that moves in near-silence. Ideal for clandestine operations.
Blue Steel's deep navy and silver colouring was inspired by deep-water environments. It incorporated early underwater operation capability — a precursor to Hammerhead.
The Piston's hydraulic actuator frame delivers enormous kinetic strikes, designed to breach fortified structures and demolish heavy machinery.
Red and white with clean geometric lines, the Romeo was Tony's most refined Legion aesthetic — a suit he reportedly called his favourite to look at.
The MCU's take on the classic Silver Centurion — silver with crimson accents, the most balanced suit in the entire Legion. Tony considered it the peak of his pre-Avengers-era engineering.
An asymmetric weapons configuration with a heavily reinforced left arm for close-quarters combat. Tony was testing whether dominant-side loading improved reaction accuracy.
The Red Snapper featured hydraulically extending arm attachments, designed for search and rescue operations — clearing rubble and extracting trapped civilians from disaster zones.
White and blue, the Peacemaker was designed with non-lethal crowd control systems — EMP, sonic deterrents, stun repulsors. Tony's attempt at a diplomatic suit.
Tony's first fully operational underwater suit. The Hammerhead was built for deep-sea operations — pressure-hardened hull, waterproof systems, and torpedo launchers.

power_source: Dual Arc Reactor Mark II Configuration
lore: The heaviest suit Tony ever built, Igor is a walking fortress. Its dual arc reactor system and seismic anchor legs let it lift and stabilise collapsing structures. Nearly immovable when locked in place.
Tony's first space-capable suit, designed for orbital operations with vacuum sealing and cryogenic insulation. The Starboost could achieve orbital insertion under its own power.
The fastest suit of the Legion series — Mach 8.5, sacrificing armour for pure velocity. Used to intercept the falling oil rig workers in the Extremis showdown.
The lightest suit ever built by Tony — an exposed titanium skeleton with minimal surface plating. Bones trades protection for unmatched agility. Built to prove the concept of minimal mass.
Tony's primary suit during the Mandarin crisis, the Mark XLII pioneered thought-controlled assembly — individual panels flying to the wearer on neural command. It was destroyed by Killian.
Built after the events of IM3 without Tony's arc reactor implant, the Mark XLIII used an external chest piece. Destroyed by Ultron in the Avengers facility during their first confrontation.

Designed specifically to subdue the Hulk, the Hulkbuster is the most physically imposing suit in Tony's arsenal. Worn over the Mark XLIII, it can replace its own damaged parts mid-combat via an orbital support pod.
Worn during the Sokovia crisis, the Mark XLV held a city in the sky. Destroyed in the battle when Ultron's sentries overwhelmed Tony's position above the floating city fragment.
Worn during the Avengers' civil war, the Mark XLVI battled both Captain America and Bucky Barnes simultaneously. Severely damaged during the Siberia confrontation.
Running FRIDAY as its primary AI, the Mark XLVII was Tony's go-to suit during the Spider-Man mentorship period. Intercepted the hijacked Stark cargo plane over the Atlantic.
A transitional suit bridging conventional construction and Tony's nanotech research. Worn briefly before Tony completed the Mark L's nanotech integration.
The first suit to incorporate partial nanotechnology, the Mark XLIX was a proof-of-concept for the fully nano-integrated Mark L that followed.

Stored entirely within Tony's arc reactor chest piece, the Mark L deploys as a wave of nanobots that assemble the suit around him in under a second. It can reconfigure into any weapon or tool on demand. Sustained heavy damage from Thanos on Titan.
Tony's first post-Infinity War build, developed during his self-imposed retirement. The beginning of a five-year engineering evolution in a lakeside cabin.
Built during Tony's early quantum realm research, the Quantum incorporated shielding designed to protect against temporal displacement effects.
Built for the lake behind his cabin, the Aqua was Tony's most advanced underwater suit yet — nanotech that could reconfigure in real-time for aquatic operations.
Tony's most advanced stealth suit — nanotech with active radar absorption and minimal arc reactor emission. Near-invisible to both optical and electronic detection.
The cabin era's Igor equivalent — heavy lifting, disaster response, and structural support. Built with nanotech for adaptable tool configurations.
An aerodynamics research suit pushing the limits of fluid-dynamic nanotech skin. Drift could reshape its exterior profile mid-flight to optimise for any speed or angle.
The Meridian was Tony's AI research platform — a suit built primarily to push the limits of FRIDAY's combat prediction systems and multi-spectrum threat analysis.
The first suit powered by Tony's redesigned Mark V arc reactor, the Crucible ran hotter and hit harder than anything he'd built since Bleeding Edge.
Tony's first suit to integrate vibranium-threaded nanotech composites, dramatically increasing the suit's structural integrity and energy absorption capacity.
Tony's penultimate pre-Endgame design, the Sentinel achieved near-perfect AI-suit symbiosis. Five years of quiet engineering converging toward one final design.

Tony Stark's final suit. Built across five years of retirement, the Mark LXXXV incorporated vibranium-nanotech composites and housed a custom Infinity Gauntlet. Tony used it to undo Thanos's snap — and sacrificed his life to do it.
James Rhodes appropriated Tony's Mark II and had it retrofitted by Justin Hammer with a weapons platform: minigun, missile batteries, and military-grade firepower. The birth of War Machine.
The War Machine armour repainted in red, white, and blue as a PR rebranding exercise by the US government. Hijacked by Aldrich Killian's Extremis soldiers to abduct the President.
A fully redesigned War Machine with upgraded weapons systems and improved manoeuvrability. Severely damaged in Civil War when Vision accidentally shot it down during the airport battle.
The same Mark III saw Rhodes through his rehabilitation after Civil War. Tony built Rhodey an exoskeleton to help him walk again — a debt repaid in iron.
The War Machine suit upgraded with partial nanotech construction, giving Rhodes on-demand weapons reconfiguration. Fought in the Battle of Wakanda against Thanos's army.
The Mark VI brought Rhodey's War Machine into the nanotech era with full weapons reconfiguration. Fought in the final battle against 2014-Thanos's army at the destroyed Avengers compound.
Built by Tony for Pepper Potts — gold and rose-gold nanotech with a focus on protection and rescue over firepower. Pepper wore it in the final battle against Thanos, declaring herself Rescue.
Tony's first dedicated stealth suit, built in 1981 for covert infiltration. Radar-absorbent plating and a suppressed power signature made it near-invisible to Cold War detection systems.
A significant evolution of the stealth concept, the Mark II introduced active camouflage — bending light around the suit's surface for near-visual invisibility.
The pinnacle of pre-nanotech stealth engineering. The Mark III suppressed radar, sonar, thermal, and optical signatures simultaneously — effectively a ghost in the machine.

The comics Silver Centurion debuted in Iron Man #200, the issue Tony defeated Obadiah Stane. Silver with red accents, it was Tony's most advanced suit of the era — and the one he wore to win back his company.
Tony's first dedicated space suit, designed in 1981 for operations beyond Earth's atmosphere. Its solar-augmented reactor replenished energy during orbital missions.
Built specifically to stop Thor when he went rogue enforcing his worldview on humanity. Powered by a crystal charged with the Odinforce, it was strong enough to wound the God of Thunder — briefly.
After taking the Extremis virus, Tony integrated the suit's undersheath into his own biology — stored in his bones, deployable via direct neural command. Man and machine became one.

Inspired by alien symbiote biology, the Endo-Sym responds to Tony's thoughts without any digital interface — it is psychoreactive living metal that anticipates its wearer. Worn during the darker Superior Iron Man period.
The most versatile suit in comics history — Model Prime can reconfigure into any Iron Man armour that has ever existed, or into entirely new forms, in real time. One suit. Infinite configurations.
Built to fight the Celestials — cosmic beings who judge entire planets. The Godkiller is Tony's answer to the question: what do you build to kill a god? It's the size of a space station.
A refined Godkiller with improved quantum-dark energy systems and a lighter hull. Built to address the weaknesses of the original in Tony's ongoing war against the Celestials.
After absorbing Celestial power during the Godkiller mission, Tony briefly became Iron God — a being of near-unlimited energy. The most powerful Tony Stark has ever been. It did not last.

When Tony's morality was inverted by the Scarlet Witch, his Superior Iron Man suit reflected the change — full-white Endo-Sym armour wielded by a Tony Stark with no ethical constraints. Eventually destroyed when he was reverted.
